title: Organizing your project folder
content:
An animatic quickly turns into a lot of files: image sequences from several cameras, Blender files, audio and After Effects projects. In this part you'll set up a project folder with a place for each, and see a naming convention for rendered image sequences that tells you which camera and which frames each one holds. It pays off when you start moving image sequences into After Effects, and again when you swap the animatic's renders for final ones.

Check your Blender version

  1. Find the version number. 0:00 The video uses Blender 2.91. Anything from 2.8 on is easy to follow; older versions have most of the same features but a very different interface. Blender shows its version at the bottom right of the window 0:23: if a button isn't where the video has it, check which version you're comparing against.

Give every kind of file a folder

  1. Make a project folder with a folder for each kind of file. 0:41 Because you'll make so many files, be strict about naming and about where everything goes. The project folder in the video, animatic, holds aftereffects, animatic-renders, audio, blender, final-renders and videos.

  2. Keep the After Effects projects together. 0:58 The aftereffects folder is where the audio is edited and the shots are cut together, so it holds the After Effects project files. A folder that After Effects made on its own, left at the top of the project, goes in here too 1:22.

Name image sequences by camera and frames

  1. Put each render in a folder named for its camera and frame range. 1:12 animatic-renders holds the image sequences from Blender's viewport render (coming in a later part), one folder each. Each name starts with the camera it was rendered from: cam-1_1-144 is camera 1, frames 1 to 144 2:08.

  2. Render more than one range from a camera when you need to. 1:45 You might want different parts of the timeline as separate image sequences, or come up with more animation after the main shot is done and add it at the end of the timeline. Here, cam-1_144-192 is extra animation added after the fact, while cam-2_1-144 and cam-3_1-144 cover the same frames as camera 1: the whole main animation 2:29.

  3. Mark shots you've slowed down. 3:11 cam-3_250-350_x400 is frames 250 to 350, which don't match the others, and x400 means it was time remapped. Time remapping speeds up or slows down a finished animation by changing the frames it happens on.

  4. Find Time Remapping. 3:37 It's in Output Properties, under the frame start, end, step and frame rate. With Old at 100 and New at 400, every 100 frames become 400: the animation plays four times slower 4:00. Taking a part of camera 3's animation and slowing it down moved it from somewhere in frames 1 to 144 to frames 250 to 350 4:41. x400 is just a convention for remembering that; you'll see how it works when the animation is looked at later in the series.

    Time Remapping is called Time Stretching. It's in Output Properties → Frame Range, with the same Old and New values.

  5. Burn the details into the images. 5:29 Each image in the sequence has its details burned in: a timestamp, the frame number and the camera. Step through the images (the video previews them in Finder and presses ↓) and the frame number printed on the image matches the file's number 5:52. Setting this up comes later in the series.

Keep everything else in its place

  1. Put audio and Blender files in their folders. 6:10 All the audio you use goes in audio, and every .blend file goes in blender, including any autosave files lying around 6:14.

  2. Give final renders the same names as the animatic renders. 6:17 Keep a separate folder for each kind of render. The folders and files in final-renders are named the same as in animatic-renders: they're the same shots, just rendered at higher quality. That lets you drop them in and replace the animatic's images in your After Effects edit as you fine-tune your animation 6:49.

  3. Keep exported videos in videos. 7:01 Anything you export from After Effects, or any other software, goes in videos: here, the animatic and the final rendered version from Part 1.

7:16 Next, you'll open the scene file and start animating.
